title: Why Airplane Windows Have A Tiny Hole
text:
That tiny hole in the airplane window isn't a flaw. It's doing a job.

Cabin windows are built with three panes. The outer pane holds most of the pressure difference between the freezing sky outside and the pressurized cabin inside. A small bleed hole sits in the middle pane and quietly equalizes pressure between the panes, so the outer one takes the strain instead of the inner one facing passengers.

It also keeps the middle pane dry, which is why the window rarely fogs up, even at 35,000 feet.
